### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. autosomal dominant childhood-onset proximal spinal muscular atrophy without contractures  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.781)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2961)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in DYNC1H1 (HGVS:c.XXXXT>C) —DISRUPTS→ DYNC1H1 (HGNC:2961); DYNC1H1 (HGNC:2961) —DISRUPTS→ Axonal transport (GO:0008085); Axonal transport (GO:0008085) —LEADS_TO→ Muscle weakness (HP:0001324); Axonal transport (GO:0008085) —LEADS_TO→ Proximal muscle atrophy (HP:0003701). Pathogenic variants in DYNC1H1 lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting axonal transport. Impaired axonal transport affects motor neurons, ultimately resulting in muscle weakness and proximal muscle atrophy.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of pathogenic variants in DYNC1H1 in individuals with these distinct phenotypes, or identification of distinct, non-overlapping sets of genetic variants in DYNC1H1 that correlate strictly with one phenotype over the other. _(variant: Exclusion of common pathogenic variants in DYNC1H1 from gnomAD databases that are associated with these conditions.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of DYNC1H1 in these distinct neurological disorders could facilitate the development of targeted therapies aimed at restoring axonal transport or enhancing motor neuron function, potentially benefiting patients with both conditions.

#### 2. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease axonal type 2O  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.781)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:2961)

**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in DYNC1H1 (null) —DISRUPTS→ DYNC1H1 (HGNC:2961); DYNC1H1 (HGNC:2961) —DECREASES→ Neuronal development and maintenance (null); Neuronal development and maintenance (null) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Neuronal development and maintenance (null) —LEADS_TO→ Motor neuropathy (HP:0001342). Mutations in DYNC1H1 lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting neuronal development and maintenance pathways, which in turn causes intellectual disability in MONDO:0013805 and motor neuropathy in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease axonal type 2O.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in DYNC1H1 with a frequency greater than 1% in gnomAD exomes would refute the hypothesis that mutations in this gene are the sole cause of these distinct diseases. _(variant: gnomAD:HGNC:2961)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving DYNC1H1 provides a potential therapeutic target for both intellectual disability syndromes and axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, possibly through gene therapy or small molecule approaches aimed at restoring DYNC1H1 function or compensating for its loss.
